claims.text: The RAS events logged for compute node R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 show a consistent pattern of KERNEL FATAL data TLB error interrupts, with all 30 lines reporting the same type of error, indicating a potential issue with the node's kernel or hardware.

In contrast, the RAS events logged for node R02-M1-N0-C:J12-U11 report instruction cache parity errors, but these errors are corrected, and the node does not exhibit the same level of fatal errors as R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01.

The timing of the errors on R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 suggests a prolonged period of instability, with errors occurring over several hours, whereas the errors on R02-M1-N0-C:J12-U11 are more sporadic and occur over a longer period of time, spanning several days.
The fact that R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 experiences repeated fatal errors without any corrective action in between suggests a more severe issue with this node.

The root cause of the anomalies on R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 is that these fatal data TLB error interrupts recur without a corrective action in between, indicating a persistent problem that requires attention.
